prediction.text: Based on my recollection of ExxonMobil's risk factors rather than a line-by-line check of the filing, the 2024 10-K says greenhouse gas and other climate-related policies could raise costs and reduce demand for its products. Examples include carbon taxes, cap-and-trade systems, emissions limits, fuel-efficiency standards, and renewable fuel mandates. The company says these could make some projects and operations less economic, require added capital or compliance spending, and lower profitability and asset values. It also notes that rules differ across countries and can change quickly, which adds uncertainty to long-term investment decisions. Separately, it says that its lower-emission businesses (carbon capture, hydrogen, biofuels, lithium) and its emission-reduction goals depend partly on supportive government policy, technology development, and market demand, so a lack of that support could limit returns or progress. Climate-related litigation is flagged as an additional risk. For exact wording, check Item 1A (Risk Factors) in the filing.
